title.value: Depth with nonlinearity creates no bad local minima in ResNets
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned in the paper's abstract and header information.
title.quote: Depth with nonlinearity creates no bad local minima in ResNets

analysis.description: This paper proves that for a type of arbitrarily deep ResNets with arbitrary nonlinear activation functions, all local minima are no worse than the global minimum value of corresponding classical machine-learning models and guarantees further improvements via residual representations.

type.justification: The paper focuses on proving theoretical results about the optimization landscape of ResNets rather than conducting empirical experiments.
type.quote: This paper advances the optimization theory of deep learning only for ResNets and not for other network architectures.

name.justification: The paper addresses the theoretical optimization challenges in training deep residual networks.

name.justification: The paper specifically discusses the properties of local minima in ResNets, which are a type of neural network architecture with residual connections.
name.quote: In this paper, we prove that depth with nonlinearity creates no bad local minima in a type of arbitrarily deep ResNets with arbitrary nonlinear activation functions.

name.justification: The paper studies the optimization landscape in terms of local minima in non-convex, high-dimensional spaces typical of deep learning models.
name.quote: However, one of the major concerns in both theory and practice is that training a deep learning model requires us to deal with highly non-convex and high-dimensional optimization.
